diagnostic_evidence.quote: and use $|\cdot|_{H^{k}}$ and $|\cdot|_{W^{k,p}}$ to denote the usual Sobolev seminorms.

where we used the Sobolev embedding $H^1 \hookrightarrow L^6$ and elliptic regularity in the first step, Hölder's inequality and again the Sobolev embedding $H^1 \hookrightarrow L^6$ in the second step and Young's inequality in the third.

issues.failure_explanation: In the derivation of (energy_esti), the second step of the II-bound claims |e|_{H^1}||e||_{L^3}||e||_{L^2} <= C_S^{1/2}|e|_{H^1}^{3/2}||e||_{L^2}^{3/2} from Hölder plus H^1 -> L^6. Those tools give ||e||_{L^3} <= ||e||_{L^2}^{1/2}||e||_{L^6}^{1/2} <= C_S^{1/2}||e||_{L^2}^{1/2}||e||_{H^1}^{1/2}, and since ||e||_{H^1}^2 = ||e||_{L^2}^2 + |e|_{H^1}^2 >= |e|_{H^1}^2, the full H^1-norm cannot be replaced by the seminorm in an upper bound (the seminorm-only Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality already fails for constant e). The term C_S^{3/2}C_ell|e|_{H^1}||e||_{L^2}^2 is dropped; after Young's inequality it contributes ~8C_S^3C_ell^2 y_1^2 (y_1 = ||e||_{L^2}^2), which the printed constants of (energy_esti) cannot absorb: the |e|_{H^1}^2 budget is exactly exhausted and 8C_S^3C_ell^2 y_1^2 <= (1/8)y_1 + c_B C_S^6C_ell^4 y_1^3 requires c_B >= 128, so B = 108C_S^6C_ell^4 is too small.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry the missing term C_S^{3/2}C_ell|e|_{H^1}||e||_{L^2}^2 through Young's inequality and absorb the resulting 8C_S^3C_ell^2 y_1^2 pointwise into the linear and cubic terms (e.g. keep the constant 1/4 in a(t) and enlarge B to 236C_S^6C_ell^4); update B in (energy_esti), (stab_cond), (root) and Theorem main_thm.
issues.overall_effect: The estimate (energy_esti) is not established with its printed constants; hence the explicit smallness conditions (stab_cond), (root) and the constant 108C_S^6C_ell^4 appearing twice in Theorem main_thm are not justified as printed, and the certified conditions and reported availability times are unreliable until the constants are corrected.
issues.title: Dropped L^2-term in the Sobolev interpolation step of the energy estimate
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local, routine rebalancing of Young-inequality constants in a single energy estimate; all statements, rates, the method and the advertised scope survive with only slightly larger explicit constants.

issues.failure_explanation: The continuation argument yields, on each interval, sup_{[t^n,t^{n+1}]} ||e||^2 + int_{t^n}^{t^{n+1}} |e|_{H^1}^2 <= Psi_n. The theorem claims sup_{[0,T]} ||e||^2 + int_0^T |e|_{H^1}^2 <= Psi_{N_t-1}. The sup-part follows since Psi_n is nondecreasing, but the dissipation integral only satisfies int_0^T |e|_{H^1}^2 = sum_n int_{t^n}^{t^{n+1}} |e|_{H^1}^2 <= sum_n Psi_n, and the recursion A_{n+1} = Psi_n + residual does not accumulate the local dissipation bounds. With comparable contributions on each of the N_t intervals the sum is about N_t times the final local bound, so the stated global bound is false in general; the valid conclusion is sup <= Psi_{N_t-1} and int_0^T |e|_{H^1}^2 <= sum_n Psi_n.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the conclusion as sup_{[0,T]} ||e||_{L^2}^2 <= Psi_{N_t-1} together with int_0^T |e|_{H^1}^2 <= sum_{n=0}^{N_t-1} Psi_n (<= N_t Psi_{N_t-1}), and adjust the estimator in Theorem main_thm ii) accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The L^2(0,T;H^1)-part of the local-in-time stability estimate and of the estimator in Theorem main_thm ii) is overclaimed by up to a factor N_t; the certified H^1-error bound is unreliable as printed. The sup-bound, and hence the a posteriori existence conclusions (cor:added-2) and the availability comparison in Table stab_comp, are unaffected.
issues.title: Global L^2(0,T;H^1) bound overclaimed by up to a factor N_t
issues.why_classification: The argument only supports the weaker summed bound, so correcting the statement necessarily loses quantitative content (up to a factor N_t on the H^1-part), but no new proof architecture is required and the sup-bound, the computability and the existence guarantees survive, leaving a recognizably comparable result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which we equip with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions and an initial condition $\rho_0 \in L^2$,
For $n=0$, we recall $\rho_h^0|_K = \rho_0(x_K)$, for all $K\in\mathcal{T}_h$, where $x_K$ denotes the circumcenter of the tetrahedron $K$.

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm initializes the piecewise constant FV solution by point evaluation rho_h^0|_K := rho_0(x_K) at the circumcenters, but the paper's standing assumption is rho_0 in L^2(Omega) (see (KScond), Theorem weakexistence, Proposition apostverif), for which point values at x_K are not defined. The initialization step is therefore ill-defined for the stated class of initial data; the same ill-defined definition is recalled in the reconstruction section.

failure_location.quote: We start by defining $\rho_h^0 \in R_h$ by $\rho_h^0|_K := \rho_0(x_K)$, for all $K \in\mathcal{T}_h$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define rho_h^0 by cell averages, rho_h^0|_K := |K|^{-1} int_K rho_0 dx (equivalently the L^2-projection onto R_h), both in Algorithm FV-FE-algo and in the recalled definition in Section Morley.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm FV-FE-algo is not well-defined under the paper's own hypotheses, so the scheme and all downstream computations (residual estimator, error bounds) are formally undefined for general L^2 initial data.
issues.title: FV-FE initialization uses point values of merely L^2 initial data
issues.why_classification: Replacing point evaluation by the standard cell-average projection is a local, routine fix that preserves the scheme, the analysis, the initial-error term in A, and every stated guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: Squaring the trace inequality (Tr) costs a factor 2: h_F^{-1}||v||_{L^2(F)}^2 <= 2 c_Tr^2 (h_F^{-2}||v||_{L^2(K)}^2 + ||grad v||_{L^2(K)}^2), via (a+b)^2 <= 2(a^2+b^2). The proof of Lemma diff-res applies it without the factor 2, and the proof of Lemma conv-res additionally splits ||M_K(phi)-M_L(phi)||^2 <= (||M_K(phi)-phi|| + ||phi-M_L(phi)||)^2 again without the factor 2. With the rest of their computation (factor 4 from the four faces), the rigorous constant in Lemma diff-res is 2 sqrt(2) c_Tr sqrt(c_usr^2 c_P^2+1), not c_R = 2 c_Tr sqrt(...); c_R' = c_Tr sqrt(12(...)) in Lemma conv-res is likewise underestimated. The stated residual bounds are therefore not rigorous with the printed constants.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the factor 2 from (a+b)^2 <= 2(a^2+b^2) when squaring (Tr) and when splitting M_K(phi)-M_L(phi), enlarging c_R to 2 sqrt(2) c_Tr sqrt(c_usr^2 c_P^2+1) and c_R' analogously, and propagate the larger constants into the estimator of Theorem main_thm.
issues.overall_effect: The face-jump contributions to the residual estimates of Lemmas diff-res and conv-res (and of diff-res0, conv-res0 by reference) are underestimated, so the fully computable residual estimator Theta in Theorem main_thm can fall below the true H^{-1}-residual; certified error bounds and existence conclusions based on the printed constants are not rigorous as stated.
issues.title: Estimator constants c_R and c_R' too small: factor 2 lost when squaring the trace inequality and splitting means
issues.why_classification: Only explicit constants in the estimator change; the correction is a routine algebraic fix with no new argument, and all qualitative claims (conditional estimates, existence, convergence rates) survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For the $\ell_1^0(t)$-terms, we first add and subtract the Morley reconstruction $\tilde{\rho}^1$ and then proceed as before.

issues.failure_explanation: For t in [t^0,t^1], the ell_1^0-part of -int P . grad phi contains, after adding and subtracting rho~^1, the term int (rho~^1 - rho~^0) grad(c~^0 - c_h^0) . grad phi, which by Hölder's inequality and the FE a posteriori bound is estimated by + ||rho~^1 - rho~^0||_{L^infty} eta_Omega^0 (exactly as term III_1 in Lemma conv-res, which enters theta_C^1 with a plus sign). Lemma conv-res0 instead claims the upper bound with the negative term - ||rho~^1 - rho~^0||_{L^infty} eta_Omega^0. Since this quantity is nonnegative, the stated bound is strictly smaller than the justified one and fails whenever the alignment term is positive; the n = 0 convective residual estimate is not valid as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign of the last term in Lemma conv-res0 to + ||rho~^1 - rho~^0||_{L^infty} eta_Omega^0 and include this term in the n = 0 contribution to the estimator in Theorem main_thm.
issues.overall_effect: The initial-time contribution to the residual estimator in Theorem main_thm can be underestimated by up to 2 ||rho~^1 - rho~^0||_{L^infty} eta_Omega^0, so the n = 0 part of the certified residual bound (and hence of A_0 and both estimators) is unreliable as printed.
issues.title: Wrong sign of the eta_Omega^0 term in the n = 0 convective residual bound
issues.why_classification: A single sign correction that slightly enlarges the estimator; the argument, all conclusions, rates and the advertised scope are preserved.
